text.title: Database Design (PostgreSQL) Output Contract
text.summary: Pins the shape of a valid Database Design (PostgreSQL) output. Subagent MUST satisfy this contract before returning to caller.

required.field: the actual answer / chosen option / value produced
at least 2 sentences; cites at least one input artefact by name
list of input names with source paths or URLs

forbidden.pattern: rationale that does not reference any input by name
inputs_used empty AND decision is not 'no-op'
duplicate artefact_id within the same store

allowed-transformations.transformation: Trim rationale to no more than 500 chars, preserving numeric claims and named tools.
Promote 'no decision yet' to status='pending' rather than fabricating a decision.
Group near-duplicate inputs, recording the group with member count.

section.title: Schema-spec contract (what the artefact describes)
section.p: The artefact above records the DECISION. This section pins the schema spec that decision produces — countable facts about the schema plus the migration strategy actually chosen.

example.note: schema_id below minLength; version is not semver; tables_count below minimum; migration_plan not in the enum; required fields missing.

list.item: A single-shot destructive migration (drop + recreate in one step).
Business logic stored as a trigger or stored procedure.
An index defined with no paired query in the workload list.
Every required field populated with a typed value
No forbidden pattern matches the output
Every FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL and CHECK is declared in DDL, not only in the ORM
Every index traces to a query in the workload sample
Migration plan is expand-only / expand-then-contract / new-schema — never add-and-drop in one release
Tables plural snake_case, columns snake_case, FKs `<singular>_id`, all constraints explicitly named
No business rule lives in a trigger or stored procedure
